text:
alisa: quick sync — did a micro-sweep on block sizes + prefetch for the GQA/MQA kernel paths on A100-80GB. trying to identify robust autotune heuristics that avoid regressions on short seqlen and still capture wins for long-running chats. notes below, pls poke. :thinking:

ben: paste of the raw microbench (shortened):
```
block,prefetch,median_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_s
32,true,10.8,24.2,2500
64,true,9.9,22.7,2700
128,true,9.6,23.0,2650
256,false,11.5,30.1,2100
64,false,11.3,27.8,2400
```

ben: summary — prefetch helps for 32/64 on mid seqlen (<=512), 128 slightly better but noisier. 256 prefers no prefetch because of larger page churn. MQA path shows slightly different crossover point (prefetch wins up to ~384).

carol: thanks. couple thoughts: 1) we should not base autotune only on median; p95 and cold-start penalty matter. 2) add a warmup-aware signal: measure 1st-token latency and then steady-state. 3) consider hardware-affine thresholds (A100 vs H100 swap point).

carol: proposed autotune rule sketch: prioritize configs where (steady_tokens_s * alpha) - (p95 * beta) is max, with alpha=1 and beta tuned by SLO class. pseudocode:
```
score = tokens_per_s * 1.0 - p95_ms * 0.01 - cold_first_ms * 0.02
choose config with max score subject to p95 < p95_slo
```

dave: FYI we observed a KV-cache layout artifact: when block size crosses 128, the paged-KV stripe allocation changes and we get a ~30% increase in memcpy during prefetch. that's why 256 regresses. also MQA introduces extra per-head bookkeeping that amplifies small-copy penalties.

dave: experiment suggestion — include a lightweight memcpy counter in the microbench and tag traces with kv_page_frag and allocator_stats. that will help autotuner avoid false wins that are actually memory thrash.

ben: added memcpy counts to the run, sample:
```
block,prefetch,memcpy_kb_per_request
32,true,120
64,true,140
128,true,380
256,false,820
```

ben: correlates with the perf drop at 128+. so we can add a regularization term in the score: -gamma * memcpy_kb.

alisa: good. another risk: routing. if smart-router switches MQA/GQA variants mid-conversation (seqlen evolves), autotune should favor stable config switches to avoid repeated cache reshuffle. maybe add hysteresis (require N requests to flip).

carol: agree. hysteresis + short-seqlen bias. practical rule: only apply a more aggressive block size if sustained improvement for 30s or 20 requests. also prefer configs that keep KV layout invariant (same stripe boundaries) to avoid re-paging cost.

dave: quick note on implementation: the kernel selector already exposes candidate_tags ("prefetch=true","blk=64","kv_layout=v2"). extend the decision API to accept a cost_fn vector: {p95, tokens_s, memcpy_kb, cold_first}. then run a tiny hill-climb at startup per-queue. keeps runtime overhead tiny.

perf-bot: CI microbench run (2167890670): baseline vs tuned-autotune-hypothesis: integrated p95 change +3.9% for seqlen<=64, -12.4% for seqlen>=512. alloc_frag spike noted for blk>=128. full logs: http://ci.redwood/bench/2167890670

alisa: action items: 1) carol to wire score fn into tuner API (small PR), 2) ben to extend bench harness with memcpy_kb + cold_first metrics, 3) dave to add kv_layout stability flag, 4) we gate rollouts with hysteresis and a short-window rollback. will try a canary tomorrow morning.

ben: I'll upload the raw CSVs to the bench bucket and tag the run.

dave: ping @eng-sre if we need to bump prefetch mem limits for the canary.

alisa: thanks, team. documenting notes here so we don't repeat the 128 cliff. :thumbsup:
